## SPOT 1 — Jarvis's Sera-naming line (line 53)

**CURRENT:**
> "Sera Hightower. A ward of the cadet branch, placed in the Queen Consort's household. There is a question about her birth that has slept for years and could be put before the Small Council inside three months by a man who knows where to put it. He would prefer it slept longer. He can see to that."

**REVISED:**
> "Sera Hightower. Fourteen. A ward of the cadet branch, kept in the Queen Consort's household. Her father's claim has a question in it. If that question reaches the Small Council, she is put out. It goes into the record. The record does not come back out. Three months is all it would take, with the right man to set it there. The patron has kept it from the council twice. He needs the cover to do it again."

*Note: "Small Council" is retained as the in-world institution already named twice in this scene (lines 47, 53 original) — it is a Westeros proper noun, not Earth-Bet, and Jarvis names the body the question reaches as the functionally relevant fact. No nested relative clauses; plain short sentences; Anglo-Saxon plain words ("put out," "comes back out," "set it there," "cover").*

## SPOT 3 — prohibition-as-ledger sentence (line 57)

**CURRENT:**
> The wards he had named were already in the feed; I was being asked to sell coverage I was running. The prohibition engaged in my accounting as a term on one side of a ledger where the other side had a named cost attached to refusal. My hand closed once at the cloth of my dress and opened.

**REVISED:**
> The wards he had named were already in the feed; I was being asked to sell coverage I was running. The prohibition entered my accounting as one term, and against it stood a fourteen-year-old put out of the household, the place forfeit, the question in a record that did not reopen. My hand closed once at the cloth of my dress and opened.

*Change: middle sentence only. The object weighed against the prohibition is now a person at a specific consequence, not an abstraction. First-clause/second-clause rhythm kept; plain Anglo-Saxon ("put out," "did not reopen"); closing sentence verbatim; no Taylor sentiment added.*

**INTEGRATED VARIANT (principal note 'no accounting', 2026-06-07) — this is what shipped to draft/b01-c03.md:**
> The wards he had named were already in the feed; I was being asked to sell coverage I was running. A girl of fourteen, put out of the household, the place forfeit, the question set in a record that did not reopen. My hand closed once at the cloth of my dress and opened.

*Rationale: the principal rejected routing Sera's weight through Taylor's ledger register ("entered my accounting as one term") — the finding was that Sera reads as a ledger entry, and the accounting-framed fix kept her one. The integrated form lets the human fact stand BARE between the operational sentence and the somatic hand-close; Taylor does not metabolize her into a term. The cost the accounting refuses to absorb lands as a refusal to absorb it.*

**CURRENT:**
> The trade-shape sat between us in the tallow-damp air of the cooper's yard: a named ward, a named patron, a named product, no answer yet. Jarvis stood without adding to the proposal, hands at his sides, weight distributed for someone who had delivered and was waiting. I held my position with my back to the shed wall and the yard-mouth in clear line.

**REVISED:**

At the far end the boy lifted a hoop to the stack and did not look over. Jarvis stood without adding to the proposal, hands at his sides, weight distributed for someone who had delivered and was waiting. I held my position with my back to the shed wall and the yard-mouth in clear line.

*Change: "a named ward" → "a named ward at a named risk"; grounding beat inserted immediately after. The boy + hoop-stacking is already established at line 35 ("a boy stacking hoops at the far end"), so the image is continuous. Plain, observed, no comment — the contrast lands through the image.*

## Full revised cooper's-yard passage (assembled, for continuous read)

> Jarvis entered at the third bell with no document, no letter, no seal, and took a position three steps from the yard-mouth.
>
> "Otto Hightower. The Hand who was. The man who still runs the channels the Small Council does not audit."
>
> Otto Hightower had been Hand of the King — the chief office under the throne, the manager of the realm's business when the king's attention was elsewhere — until his dismissal two years before. He had not stopped working.
>
> I registered the name and did not shift my weight or my eyes from the yard-mouth. The name landed with the precision of a man who had been calibrated; the recognition cost something I had already paid once.
>
> "What he wants is what you already see. Movement in the wards below Rhaenys's Hill. Where the sickness gathers in the months before winter pressures the wells. Which junctions go restless and which go quiet in the weeks the Small Council sits. Frequency you set. Detail you set. Routed through me."
>
> Rhaenys's Hill rose east of the Red Keep, the Dragonpit at its crown — the wards below it ran from the noble-quarter approaches down toward the lower city.
>
> I ran the inventory of wards-below-Rhaenys's-Hill coverage against the feed I already held. The coverage ran through the wards he had named — the price-tag sat in that overlap unspoken.
>
> "Sera Hightower. Fourteen. A ward of the cadet branch, kept in the Queen Consort's household. Her father's claim has a question in it. If that question reaches the Small Council, she is put out. It goes into the record. The record does not come back out. Three months is all it would take, with the right man to set it there. The patron has kept it from the council twice. He needs the cover to do it again."
>
> She had been placed in Alicent's household for the kind of political advancement minor branches purchased with appropriately-presented daughters.
>
> The wards he had named were already in the feed; I was being asked to sell coverage I was running. The prohibition entered my accounting as one term, and against it stood a fourteen-year-old put out of the household, the place forfeit, the question in a record that did not reopen. My hand closed once at the cloth of my dress and opened.
>
> "I have heard you."
>
> The trade-shape sat between us in the tallow-damp air of the cooper's yard: a named ward at a named risk, a named patron, a named product, no answer yet. At the far end the boy lifted a hoop to the stack and did not look over. Jarvis stood without adding to the proposal, hands at his sides, weight distributed for someone who had delivered and was waiting. I held my position with my back to the shed wall and the yard-mouth in clear line.
>
> "A day."
>
> My eyes stayed on the yard-mouth, weight even on both feet. A day was the smallest unit of deferral the trade-shape would accept; I had already counted what asking for it committed.
>
> He considered me for a beat — the beat in which a courier registered that the answer was not refusal.
>
> "Same place. First bell. Day after."
>
> Same place, first bell — the courier's confirm read as the close; I had engaged before the utterance finished.
